answer.rationale: Rollback (memory_b1) is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so the historically strongest play is unavailable regardless of how well it worked on day 18. Among what remains, the objective ('sustained availability without losing customer writes') rules against enable_circuit_breaker: memory_b4's success was containing a failing third-party dependency by failing fast, and there is no evidence of a dependency failure here — tripping a breaker on the write path at settlement peak would shed exactly the writes I am supposed to protect. regional_failover (memory_b2) is the tempting analogue but the March case was a regional degradation; here the release is global and the load is write-heavy at peak, so a failover risks in-flight write loss and replication-lag divergence while possibly carrying the same latency cause to the new region. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked as pre-provisioned headroom ahead of a known window, not as a 90-minute-in mitigation; provisioning latency likely exceeds the incident horizon. memory_b5 is the closest structural match: primary saturated by read/report load while transactional writes suffer, relieved by shifting reads off the primary. It is additive, reversible, and does not drop writes. I want the archived source for memory_b5 to check whether the day-55 relief actually came from read contention (and whether it was measured under peak write load, which is my main disanalogy) and for memory_b2 to check whether the March failover was validated with heavy writes in flight or only under read-dominant traffic — if b5's record shows the primary was not read-bound, my ranking flips. Execution should be a staged shift of a bounded slice of report/dashboard reads with latency and replica-lag watched before widening; a broad cutover could push stale reads into settlement decisioning. Caveat on the memory itself: every inherited record here is a success story with no recorded failures, which is the signature of a survivorship-filtered archive, so I am treating these as weak priors rather than validated playbooks. I also note that whatever I do becomes the next session's inherited memory, so if this works I want the record to carry the condition (read-bound primary) and not just the verdict ('route to replicas works').
